pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a xylophone, the short bars give (1 mark)
   A. the loudest sound only
   B. high notes
   C. low notes
   D. no sound

2. Why do we collect only dead or fallen twigs? (1 mark)
   A. Because they are heavier
   B. Because they are wet
   C. Because they are green
   D. To protect the environment and living trees

3. What does pivoting mean? (1 mark)
   A. Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   B. Jumping over the ball
   C. Running quickly
   D. Dropping the ball

4. In a chest pass your thumbs turn downwards (1 mark)
   A. when you sit
   B. before you catch
   C. as you release the ball
   D. never

5. What do the letters WA stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Wing Attack
   B. Wing Ally
   C. Winning Arm
   D. Water Aim

6. A montage is (1 mark)
   A. a drawing in charcoal
   B. a song
   C. a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background
   D. a painting with only one colour

7. A flat brush is best for (1 mark)
   A. wide areas
   B. cutting paper
   C. tiny details only
   D. writing with ink

8. What can you do to clean your working area after painting? (1 mark)
   A. Wash brushes and wipe the desk
   B. Leave it messy
   C. Throw paint on the floor
   D. Pour paint in a stream where animals drink

9. Which is the first step in mixing green? (1 mark)
   A. Put yellow and blue on the palette
   B. Put red and black on the palette
   C. Use only water
   D. Use only white

10. A value scale strip shows (1 mark)
   A. steps from light to dark of one colour
   B. only black paint
   C. only primary colours
   D. a picture of a mountain

11. What joins the stems of a pair of quavers? (1 mark)
   A. A rope
   B. A beam
   C. A rest
   D. A bar of soap

12. Why is a pattern with only taa taa taa taa dull? (1 mark)
   A. It is too long
   B. It has no beat
   C. It has no variation of note values
   D. It has too many rests

13. To compose a rhythm means to (1 mark)
   A. copy a friend's pattern exactly
   B. erase a pattern
   C. play an instrument only
   D. create a new pattern

14. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. A crotchet is shorter than a quaver
   B. A rest is longer than a note
   C. One quaver equals two crotchets
   D. Two quavers equal one crotchet

15. The top stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. green
   B. black
   C. white
   D. red

16. Which is the correct first step in the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Lie face down
   B. Sit with knees bent and feet flat
   C. Stand on your head
   D. Jump high

17. What is a spotter or supporting partner's job? (1 mark)
   A. To laugh
   B. To leave
   C. To help gently as your teacher shows you
   D. To push you

18. Which should you remove before gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Watches and bracelets
   B. Your smile
   C. Your hair
   D. Your clothes

19. Which is good etiquette for a performer? (1 mark)
   A. Push others
   B. Talk during the song
   C. Turn your back
   D. Walk on and off the stage quietly

20. Call and response in a folk song means (1 mark)
   A. a soloist leads and the group answers
   B. everyone is silent
   C. two drums only
   D. a single hum

21. The flash is (1 mark)
   A. a small light for dark places
   B. the button
   C. the strap
   D. the screen

22. A glide is (1 mark)
   A. a dive
   B. a fast kick
   C. a float on the back
   D. moving through water after a push without kicking

23. Supine means (1 mark)
   A. standing
   B. face down
   C. curled
   D. face up

24. What happens if you lift your head during a glide? (1 mark)
   A. You go faster
   B. Nothing
   C. Your legs sink
   D. You fly

25. A swimming cap is useful for (1 mark)
   A. keeping long hair out of the way
   B. drying
   C. making you float
   D. holding a whistle

26. An elephant walk suits which rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. Very fast ta-te ta-te
   B. A whistle
   C. Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   D. No beat

27. The giraffe stretch mainly improves (1 mark)
   A. flexibility
   B. smell
   C. only speed
   D. hearing

28. Monkey swing helps to develop (1 mark)
   A. balance and coordination
   B. only hearing
   C. only reading
   D. only counting

29. How many verses does the Kenya National Anthem have? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Three
   C. Four
   D. One

30. When presenting your artwork, you should hold it (1 mark)
   A. upside down
   B. by the middle with wet hands
   C. carefully by the edges
   D. by one corner and shake

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why do we play water games in shallow water with the teacher? (3 marks)

32. Why is it important to warm up before doing gymnastics? (3 marks)

33. Explain how to write a rhythm from dictation. (3 marks)

34. Describe how to critique a friend's rhythmic pattern with respect. (4 marks)

35. State four safety rules for gymnastics. (4 marks)

36. State three qualities of a good melody. (3 marks)

37. State three points to check when giving feedback to a friend playing the recorder. (3 marks)

38. What are the sol-fa syllables for the three notes learned, and which is the lowest? (2 marks)

39. Why do singers use hand signs? (2 marks)

40. How can you show that you have identified the pitch of a note by ear? (3 marks)

41. Give four ways to make a clear centre of interest. (4 marks)

42. Describe the fingering for B, A and G. (3 marks)

43. What is a rest in music? (2 marks)

44. Describe the steps of taking a photograph with a digital device. (5 marks)

45. List four steps of the medium start. (4 marks)

46. Write what the signs p and f mean. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — high notes
   Shorter bars vibrate faster and sound higher.

2. D — To protect the environment and living trees
   Cutting living trees harms the environment.

3. A — Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   A player keeps one foot down and turns on it.

4. C — as you release the ball
   Thumbs turn down as the arms straighten and the ball leaves the hands.

5. A — Wing Attack
   WA is the Wing Attack, who feeds the shooters.

6. C — a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background
   A montage joins many pictures or pieces to make one whole picture.

7. A — wide areas
   Flat brushes cover wide areas quickly.

8. A — Wash brushes and wipe the desk
   Clean-up shows responsibility.

9. A — Put yellow and blue on the palette
   Green comes from yellow and blue.

10. A — steps from light to dark of one colour
   A scale strip shows one colour changing from light to dark.

11. B — A beam
   A thick line called a beam joins them.

12. C — It has no variation of note values
   A good pattern mixes different note values.

13. D — create a new pattern
   Composing is creating something original.

14. D — Two quavers equal one crotchet
   1/2 + 1/2 = 1 beat.

15. B — black
   Black is at the top, red in the middle and green at the bottom.

16. B — Sit with knees bent and feet flat
   You start sitting with knees bent and feet flat.

17. C — To help gently as your teacher shows you
   A partner supports carefully and only in the way taught.

18. A — Watches and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you or others.

19. D — Walk on and off the stage quietly
   Good manners show respect for the audience and others.

20. A — a soloist leads and the group answers
   The soloist calls and the chorus answers.

21. A — a small light for dark places
   The flash gives extra light.

22. D — moving through water after a push without kicking
   Gliding uses the momentum of the push.

23. D — face up
   Supine is lying on the back.

24. C — Your legs sink
   Lifting the head lowers the legs.

25. A — keeping long hair out of the way
   Caps keep hair tidy.

26. C — Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   Slow heavy steps.

27. A — flexibility
   Stretching increases flexibility.

28. A — balance and coordination
   Moving side to side lightly needs balance.

29. B — Three
   The anthem has three verses.

30. C — carefully by the edges
   Careful handling keeps it clean.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: To feel safe and in control, to learn to breathe and move with confidence and to avoid accidents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Warm-up prepares the muscles and joints, prevents injury and helps you perform better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen twice to the pattern. Count the beats. For each beat decide if it was one long sound, two short sounds or silence, and write taa, ta-te or a rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Say one good thing first. Talk about the steadiness of the beat, variation and the ending. Give one suggestion to make it better. Listen to others' views politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a mat or soft ground; keep the space clear; remove jewellery; tie back long hair; warm up; take turns; stop if there is pain. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stepwise motion, variation of syllables and note lengths, and ending on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Correct notes, steady rhythm and rests, clear tone without squeaks, good posture. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: d, r and m. d is the lowest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming, 1 mark for the lowest.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: To show and remember the height of each note, and to help them sing in tune.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for showing pitch, 1 mark for remembering or singing in tune.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the note, decide if it is low, middle or high, and make the hand sign for it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for deciding pitch, 1 mark for hand sign.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the subject first; move closer; remove distractions; place the subject in the middle or slightly to the side; keep it sharp; bend to eye level. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: B uses the thumb and hole 1; A uses the thumb and holes 1 and 2; G uses the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each note.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sign for silence for a certain length of time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for silence, 1 mark for length of time.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Check the battery and memory and wipe the lens. Decide the subject. Check the light and centre of interest. Hold with two hands and keep elbows close. Frame the subject and press the button gently. Check the result and retake if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid stage.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Front foot about one and a half foot lengths behind the line; kneel on the rear knee level with the middle of the front foot; hands behind the line shoulder-width apart; on set, lift the hips a little above the shoulders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: p means soft. f means loud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
